The ribonucleoprotein is the **signal recognition particle (SRP)**. It binds an ER-targeting signal sequence as the nascent protein emerges from a cytosolic ribosome, temporarily pauses translation, and delivers the ribosome–nascent-chain complex to the **rough ER**. The “sugar” refers to glycosylation in the secretory pathway, after which a secreted protein proceeds through the Golgi to the extracellular space.

Strictly, an SRP signal does not guarantee secretion—it can also produce membrane or organelle-resident proteins—but among the choices, only the cytosol-to-extracellular-space route is consistent.

Answer: C
